care.summary: Brazilian epiphytic cactus with segmented flat stems and vibrant winter blooms in pink, red, white, or purple. Easy-care holiday plant that can live decades with proper conditions.
care.light: Bright, indirect light. An east-facing window is ideal. Avoid harsh midday sun, which can bleach or redden the segments.
care.water: Water thoroughly when the top 1-2 cm of soil is dry. Reduce watering after flowering and during summer dormancy; resume regular watering when buds form in autumn.
care.soil: Well-draining mix; cactus soil amended with perlite or orchid bark for aeration. Container must drain freely to prevent root rot.
care.humidity: Moderate (40-60%). Benefits from occasional misting in dry indoor air, especially when buds are setting.
care.fertilizer: Diluted balanced liquid feed every 2-4 weeks during active growth (spring/summer). Stop feeding 4 weeks before expected bloom.
care.toxicity: Non-toxic to cats, dogs, and humans. Safe around pets and children.
common_issues: Bud drop from sudden temperature change, drafts, or overwatering
Root rot in heavy or waterlogged soil
Reddened segments from too much direct sun
Failure to bloom if daylight/night cycle is interrupted by artificial light
tips: To trigger blooming, provide 12-14 hours of uninterrupted darkness and cooler temperatures (12-15 C) for 6 weeks in autumn
Once buds form, do not rotate the pot or move the plant; buds drop if conditions change
After flowering, prune by removing a few segments at the joints to encourage branching
Prefers being slightly pot-bound; repot only every 2-3 years in spring after bloom
